stem: A tailor buys an industrial sewing machine for 72,000 dollars. For tax purposes, the value \(V(t)\), in dollars, of the machine \(t\) years after it is bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 72{,}000 - 4{,}500t\). The graph of \(y = V(t)\) in the \(ty\)-plane has a \(t\)-intercept at \((16, 0)\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of this \(t\)-intercept?

choices.A: According to the model, the value of the machine decreases by 16 dollars each year.
choices.B: According to the model, the value of the machine is 72,000 dollars 16 years after it is bought.
choices.C: According to the model, the value of the machine is 4,500 dollars 16 years after it is bought.
choices.D: According to the model, the value of the machine is 0 dollars 16 years after it is bought.

solution: A \(t\)-intercept is a point where \(y = V(t) = 0\).
\(V(16) = 72{,}000 - 4{,}500(16) = 0\), so 16 years after the purchase the machine's modeled value is 0 dollars.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The yearly decrease is the coefficient 4,500 dollars; 16 is a number of years.
explanation.B: Incorrect. 72,000 dollars is the value at \(t = 0\) (the \(y\)-intercept); at \(t = 16\) the value is 0.
explanation.C: Incorrect. 4,500 dollars is the yearly decrease, not a value; \(V(16) = 72{,}000 - 4{,}500(16) = 0\).
explanation.D: Correct. At the \(t\)-intercept, \(V(16) = 0\): the input is 16 years and the output is a value of 0 dollars.

verify:
t = symbols('t')
V = 72000 - 4500*t
assert solve(V, t) == [16]
key = 'is 0 dollars 16 years'
assert key in choices[answer]
assert sum(key in c for c in choices.values()) == 1
